atoms.text: The ash is one of the most common types of tree in the UK. Ash trees usually grow to 12 - 18 metres tall. They can be found all throughout mainland Europe, as well as in the UK and Ireland.
atoms.sound: The ash is one of the most common types of tree in the UK. Ash trees usually grow to 12 to 18 metres tall. They can be found all throughout mainland Europe, as well as in the UK and Ireland.

atoms.text: Ash trees usually don’t live for longer than 250 years, although they can live up to 300 years. One of the oldest ash trees in the UK can be found at Clapton Court in Somerset. Ash trees are classed as ancient when they reach 225 years old.
atoms.sound: Ash trees usually don’t live for longer than 250 years, although they can live up to 300 years. One of the oldest ash trees in the UK can be found at Clapton Court in Somerset. Ash trees are classed as ancient when they reach 225 years old.

atoms.text: Ash trees are deciduous, which means they lose their leaves in winter. The leaves on an ash tree grow from May onwards. This helps other ground plants to grow too. When the leaves fall in autumn, they are usually a dull green or yellow colour.
